Kitchen ticket printing

This page is for a new teammate on the bakery order system. You will know how a paid order becomes a printed kitchen ticket and where to look when one does not print.

flowchart TD
  buyer(["customer"]) --> site
  subgraph cloud["cloud box"]
    site("order site") --> db[("orders table")]
    db --> q@{ shape: h-cyl, label: "ticket queue" }
  end
  subgraph shop1["north shop"]
    r1("print relay") --> p1("kitchen printer")
  end
  subgraph shop2["south shop"]
    r2("print relay") --> p2("kitchen printer")
  end
  q --> r1
  q --> r2

Each shop runs its own print relay, so one shop's broken printer never stops the other shop's tickets.

What happens to one order

StepWho actsWhat changes
1. payorder sitethe order row turns paid
2. queueorder siteone ticket joins the shop's queue
3. printprint relaythe printer prints and the ticket turns printed
4. retryprint relaya failed ticket tries again after 30 s

A ticket that fails three times stays in the queue as stuck. The shop sees it in red on the order screen.

The tables

TableKey fieldsWritten byRead by
ordersorder_id, shop_id, statusorder siteorder screen
ticketsticket_id, order_id, triesorder site, print relayprint relay

The queue is the tickets table read in order of ticket_id, so no second store exists.

Check it on the live system

Ask the order site for the stuck tickets of one shop. An empty list means every ticket printed.

curl -s https://orders.example/api/tickets?shop=north&status=stuck
[]

PartFile

the stuck-ticket countsite/screens/orders.ts:118
Why the relay runs in each shop

A relay in the cloud box would lose every shop's tickets during one network drop. A relay in each shop keeps printing from its own copy of the queue.
